mission.title: ARES PATHFINDER / CREWED MARS SURFACE MISSION
mission.objective: Design, validate, and launch a four-person Mars architecture with closed-loop life support, surface power, and oxygen ISRU.
mission.architectureNote: The 500-day stay and split cargo/crew context are adapted from NASA Mars DRA 5.0. This game's four-person vehicle, budget, masses, and launch stack are fictional gameplay scenarios.

exercises.title: Trans-Mars injection mass ratio
exercises.prompt: Scenario burn: Δv = 3,600 m/s, Isp = 350 s, g₀ = 9.80665 m/s². Calculate initial mass / final mass.
exercises.hint: Multiply Isp by g₀, divide Δv by that result, then raise e to that power.
exercises.evidence: NASA equation; Δv is a labeled gameplay scenario. NASA Glenn gives 350 s as a reasonable liquid hydrogen/liquid oxygen example.

exercises.title: Surface food energy
exercises.prompt: NASA baseline: 3,035 kcal per crewmember-day. For 4 crew over 500 days, calculate total food energy.
exercises.evidence: NASA-STD-3001 requirement combined with the DRA-inspired 500-day gameplay scenario.

exercises.title: Mars communication autonomy
exercises.prompt: NASA research cites up to 44 minutes round-trip latency at maximum Earth–Mars distance. Calculate the one-way delay available to a single message.
exercises.hint: A round trip contains two equal light-time legs.
exercises.evidence: Published NASA human-systems research; actual delay changes continuously with planetary geometry.
